video_title: This SUPER FAST 2.0 Log Bait Cycle is BUSTED!!

The building otherwise stays in hand all game (HUD reads it in hand through most of clock 2:51-0:40, low confidence): every earlier defence is Skeletons, Ice Spirit, Electro Spirit and Dart Goblin instead, which is what keeps him cycling to the Evo Goblin Barrel.

bullets: Game 5 of 7 in a single-deck video; win against a Splashyard control deck (Graveyard, Tombstone, Tornado, Barbarian Barrel, Ice Wizard, Baby Dragon, Knight, Magic Archer), video time 694.9-871.9s. 'Beautiful and GG's. Nice win' (t=866), enemy left tower ground to 127 while his own left loses under 1000.

Fixed opening: 'my favorite starting play with this deck is just split wall breakers or goblin barrel on the tower just to get to my Evo right away' (t=701-707) — the first two plays of the readable window are a barrel at clock 2:50 and bridge Wall Breakers at clock 2:40.

Evolution slots are Goblin Barrel and Dart Goblin, and he argues the Dart Goblin choice explicitly: 'you guys can use the Evo wall breakers in here over the Evo dart goblin if you would like, but I just think that the Evo dart goblin just helps you out so much on defense that there's no point really to not use it' (t=707-718).

Every offensive commitment is timed off the opponent's cycle rather than off elixir: 'because he doesn't have a tombstone in cycle' (t=744), 'he might have to waste his tombstone, and if he wastes his tombstone, then we can maybe get a good set of wall breakers shortly' (t=782-786), 'cuz he has no barb barrel in cycle' (t=838).

Defence is deliberately spirit-and-skeleton cheap so the 2.0 average keeps recycling the Evo barrel — the Cannon is only placed once, at clock 0:39 (t=852.9). By clock 1:52 and 0:52 the opponent is locked out: 'He can't even go in for a graveyard, and his cycle is completely messed up here' (t=753) and 'His cycle is absolutely cooked right now' (t=813).

The pattern he repeats to close the game is Berserker at the bridge plus Evo Goblin Barrel, with Wall Breakers behind: 'we can go for the berserker plus evo barrel and then wall breakers' (t=810-812) and again at t=836-838; the enemy left tower falls 2527 -> 127 between clock 0:48 and 0:44.

new_deck.rationale: Goblin Barrel is the win condition and Dart Goblin, Skeletons and the two spirits bait the small spells that would answer it, while a 2.0 average cost lets the Evolution barrel come back around faster than the opponent's answers.
new_deck.why_it_works_md: At 2.0 average elixir the deck outcycles anything that answers the Goblin Barrel, which is why Ryley frames the whole match around getting back to the Evolution: "All we need is to get to the next evo barrel and we'll be completely chilling" (t=832-834). The Evo Goblin Barrel and Evo Dart Goblin do the damage, Berserker and Wall Breakers add two more cheap bridge threats that force a second answer, and defence is handled almost entirely by Skeletons, Ice Spirit, Electro Spirit and Dart Goblin so the Cannon can be saved for the one push that really needs it. Because every threat is 2-3 elixir, he can attack whenever a specific opponent card is out of rotation rather than when he is ahead on elixir — in this match he counts the opponent's Tombstone and Barbarian Barrel out of cycle and barrels into the hole each time. The weakness is that nothing in the deck kills a tower on its own: the enemy left tower survived on 127 hitpoints and the win came on accumulated damage, not a crown.
